plan_a_advantages: More consistent volume of easy running
Focus on hill work, which is relevant to trail running
plan_b_advantages: Incorporates threshold interval training for speed development
Includes a longer, dedicated long run for endurance building
Adds cross-training for recovery and variation
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates more targeted intensity work, specifically threshold intervals, which directly addresses the goal of increasing speed. Plan A, while consistent, relies heavily on easy runs and hill work, which are important but don't provide the same stimulus for improving running pace. Plan B’s inclusion of longer, sustained efforts alongside the interval sessions will build both aerobic capacity and the ability to maintain a faster pace over longer distances, crucial for trail running success. Furthermore, the cross-training session in Plan B offers a valuable recovery and variation that Plan A lacks.
